Subject: Questions: logs, retention, and cross-border handling for DPF/DPA annex

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the initial materials. Our security and privacy team has a few follow-ups specifically around operational logs and how those interact with the DPF / DPA annex. High-level items we need clarified before we proceed with procurement:

- What exact categories of logs are retained for hosted API requests (request/response payloads, routing/kvs, auth/access logs, audit trails)?
- Retention defaults and configuration options (can we set custom retention per account or per route? Is 90 days available?)
- Do logs contain raw prompts or full responses by default, or are those redacted/hashed?
- How are K/V cache entries treated in logs (persisted or ephemeral only)?
- Cross-border concerns: if we route inference through US-hosted clusters, what contractual and technical safeguards do you provide for EU-origin data (DPF mapping, encryption, SCCs/alternatives)?
- Can you provide a short redacted sample of operational logs (no real PII) so our ops team can validate schema and SIEM ingestion?
- Any SOC 2 artifacts or attestation pointers relevant to logs and retention controls?

If you could respond with short, concrete answers and attach a sample log stub we can share internally, that would help. If any of these are configurable only for Dedicated/Private deployments, please call that out.

We are on a tight timeline and would like to fold this into our security review by next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Emily Tan

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below with attachments: we included a redacted operational log sample and a draft DPA annex focused on cross-border routing. If you want more detail we can run a tech session.

- Categories retained:
  * API request metadata (timestamp, route, model, token counts)
  * Authentication & authorization events (API key usage, service accounts)
  * Routing and infra telemetry (node id, region, latency metrics)
  * Application payloads (prompt/response): hosted API retains these by default but they are subject to redaction rules below.
  * KV cache: not written to persistent logs by default — cache contents are ephemeral in memory and cleared on process eviction; we log cache hit/miss metrics only.
- Retention: default hosted API retention for payloads is 30 days.
  * Configurable per customer on Dedicated accounts; Private deployments can set policy via on-prem config.
  * We can accommodate 90-day retention for hosted API under an addendum (tradeoff: additional cost & extended breach surface).
- Redaction: Redwood applies automatic PII detectors and strips or hashes recognized identifiers from payload-level logs for hosted customers. For high-sensitivity customers we offer an opt-in pipeline that redacts at ingestion and stores only hashed token fingerprints.
- Cross-border: for EU-origin traffic routed to US clusters we provide:
  * DPA annex with routing commitments and data flow mapping (see attached draft DPA annex).
  * Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2/1.3) and at rest (AES-256).
  * For hosted: contractual safeguards (SCCs/DPF statements) + operational mapping. For Dedicated/Private you can keep processing in-region.
- SOC2 & evidence: we publish our SOC2 type II report to signed NDA partners / procurement portals; will coordinate next steps with procurement.

Attached: operational-logs-sample-stub.txt (redacted sample), dpa-annex-draft.pdf (routing & annex language).

Proposed next step: 30–45 minute technical call with your security/ops team and Karthik (technical legal) to walk through sample logs and retention tradeoffs. Karthik / Ben — are you available tomorrow or Thursday afternoon PST?

Subject: Re: Questions: logs, retention, and cross-border handling for DPF/DPA annex

Emily — a few technical points to supplement Marissa's notes (keeping short, happy to expand on call):

- Payload retention specifics: hosted API keeps request/response payloads (for debugging and quality monitoring) for 30 days by default. Customers can request a retention override; for production SLAs we typically suggest Dedicated with configurable retention windows.
- Redaction & determinism: our ingestion pipeline runs a token-level PII classifier; recognized entities are replaced with stable hashes (so analytics can still group tokens without restoring original PII). For customers that require no raw prompt retention we offer an ingestion filter that discards payloads after tokenization and persists only derived metrics.
- KV cache: KV is stored in-process or on local NVMe cache on GPUs; we do not persist KV content to central object storage and do not include KV values in operational logs. We do log anonymized cache metrics (hit/miss rates, eviction counts).
- Cross-border controls: for DPF mapping we provide an exported mapping that lists processing locations, subprocessors, and contractual safeguards. For EU->US transfers we can offer:
  * SCCs (European Commission standard contractual clauses) executed as part of our DPA annex, or
  * A documented DPF assessment summary if you need a data-transfer impact narrative.
- Key management: Hosted: keys managed by Redwood KMS; customer key-scoped encryption is available for Dedicated and Private. For Private we can integrate with your HSM or KMS (see kms-integration-note.txt).

Runbook link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/abc123-runbook (contains log schemas, retention flag examples, and SIEM ingestion examples).

If you want us to produce a 10–15 row redacted CSV of sample logs formatted for Splunk/Elastic ingestion point us at the required schema and we'll generate it.

-Karthik
